MINUTES
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MARCH 24, 2025

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER
  A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order by CHAIR SCHMITZ at 7:02 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

  2.  PRESENTATION
  CHAIR SCHMITZ introduced herself as the new Chair of the Equestrian Committee.
  3.  ROLL CALL
  Committee Members Present:  Brtis, Griggs, Harik, Nilsen, Shinn, Pope,
  Romanelli, Schmitz
  Committee Members Absent:  Martin, Silvano
  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  A.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 18, 2024

  MEMBER BRTIS moved, seconded by MEMBER GRIGGS to:

  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES  OF  NOVEMBER  18,  2024,
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  There being no objection, CHAIR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

  NONE.
  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  EQUINE EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided a brief overview of the item.

  She reported that the Equine Emergency Preparedness Subcommittee had met
  and will continue to meet to review ongoing initiatives. She noted the Equine
  Preparedness page available on the City's website, and the Equine Emergency

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  1
March 24, 2024
   Preparedness brochure as items completed over the last year. She stated that City
  staff provided a presentation on preparedness to the Palos Verdes Peninsula
  Horsemen's Association in February (PVPHA) and shared that PVPHA was offering
  an upcoming microchipping clinic. ACM Davis noted that plans are underway to
  coordinate another trailering clinic in about a year as well as plans to develop an
  updated horse census for emergency preparedness purposes, which will include
  the number of horses per property and contact information.

  MEMBER GRIGGS stated that the Peninsula had been downgraded as a fire
  hazard area.

  MEMBER SHINN emphasized the importance of the horse census for evacuation
  purposes.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ highlighted the importance of microchipping horses for
  identification in emergency situations. She also commended the City's emergency
  preparedness team for their collaboration and lessons learned from other incidents.

  MEMBER NIELSEN suggested including other farm animals in the census that
  could be easily loaded into a car during evacuations. ACM Davis responded that
  the item could be added for consideration in future discussions.

  B.  OVERVIEW OF ARENA RULES, CLINICS AND LESSONS (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item. She reported on the
  process for horse trainers renting facilities for clinics, rules for trainers using arenas
  (including time limits and number of trainers and students allowing in a ring), the
  different categories of trainer licenses and permits (including fees and restrictions)
  and rental fees for the Ernie Howlett Park Equestrian Center. Supervisor Pinuelas
  stated that staff was looking for guidance and direction from the Committee as to if
  any changes are needed to how clinics are currently administered.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the trainer permit fee is meant to cover the costs of
  facilitating the horse trainer program and the City property use fee is meant to help
  offset the costs of arena maintenance, in response to MEMBER GRIGGS regarding
  regular horse training operation.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ provided an overview of the historical context regarding the
  development of the current categories and fees. She explained that, at that time,
  the Committee aimed to avoid discouraging renowned trainers from providing
  instruction to the community or limiting equestrians’ access to that training by
  making it prohibitive for a day of instruction. She also noted that the Committee
  wanted to ensure that trainers with access to private arenas would conduct their
  business in those arenas rather than the public ones, while still providing
  opportunities for those without private arenas who train regularly and resulting in
  the existing categories.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  2
March 24, 2024
   In response to MEMBER ROMANELLI, ACM Davis stated that specific to clinicians,
  or trainers who do not necessarily fit in the trainer categories, there is a challenge
  because while they are getting a business license, they are not always reserving
  an arena because the arenas are able to remain open to others not participating in
  the clinic. She added that other equestrians may not realize they can access the
  arena when these clinics are being conducted as it could appear to be rented.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that at the last meeting there was a concern regarding
  whether or not one-day trainers should also be reserving arenas in addition to the
  one-day business license.

  MEMBER ROMANELLI asked if it is a matter of enforcement as opposed to
  changing the rules and categories. Supervisor Pinuelas explained that currently
  reservations are only required if the trainer wants to limit access to the arena or if
  they plan on instructing longer than two hours consecutively based on the existing
  arena rules. She stated that some trainers want to rent the arena while others plan
  on teaching for less than two hours consecutively, consistent with the established
  rules.

  Discussion ensued regarding the frequency of violations and the ability to enforce
  the rules.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ expressed concern that if the rules were too complex it may affect
  the ability to enforce them.

  MEMBER HARIK stated that trainers wanting to keep others out of the arena should
  rent it. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that staff clarifies to trainers that unless the
  arena is rented, they cannot prevent others from using it simultaneously, nor can
  they prevent anyone from using an adjacent arena. She added that trainers are also
  made aware that the arenas are only prepped for clinics when rented.

  Discussion ensued regarding fees and business license tax charged to one-day
  trainers.

  The COMMITTEE agreed that the current system was working well and no changes
  to the administration of clinics or fees were needed at this time.

  C.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER HAYRIDES UPDATE (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided a brief overview of the item.

  She reported that Peter Weber Equestrian Center (PWEC) hayrides had been
  suspended for approximately a year and a half as a result of restrictions on Palos
  Verdes landfill site activities. She stated that the City has been collaborating with

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  3
March 24, 2024
   various Los Angeles County departments to facilitate the reinstatement of the
  hayrides. ACM Davis reported that an agreement is being drafted to permit access
  to the outer landfill loop trail as well as certain restricted roads for the purpose of
  conducting the hayrides. She stated that the item is scheduled to be presented to
  the Parks and Activities Commission next month, after which it will be forwarded to
  the City Council along with an agreement for approval. She noted that the hayrides
  would be reestablished with the understanding that they would be conducted safely
  and invited the Committee to share any questions or concerns. Chantal Allyn, an
  operator from PWEC, was in attendance to answer any questions.

  Discussion ensued regarding safety concerns and the importance of the ability to
  conduct the hayrides on the landfill. Ms. Allyn addressed concerns about safety and
  noise, assuring the Committee that experienced drivers would be used and safety
  precautions would be taken.

  D.  2025 HORSE TRAINER LIST AND PERMIT UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update regarding the 2025 Licensed Horse
  Trainer List. She reported that almost all trainers had completed the renewal
  process with two trainers yet to renew or confirm plans to do so, and two trainers
  confirmed they would not be renewing. She noted that updated trainer lists were
  posted at the arenas earlier in the month and an annual trainers meeting is
  scheduled to take place within the next couple of months.

  E.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS LIST

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item (as per the agenda
  material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the list is presented to the Committee annually and
  that future projects identified on the list would be considered for adoption in
  upcoming budgets. She reported that the list had been presented to the Park and
  Activities Commission as well as the City Council. She added that any additions
  proposed by the Committee would likewise be submitted for consideration in future
  budget cycles. Supervisor Pinuelas reported that the Shirley Klein Equestrian
  Recognition Project was completed in January.

  No additions or changes were proposed.

  F.  EQUESTRIAN FEES REVIEW

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item (as per the agenda
  material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that fees are presented to the Committee annually and
  had been reviewed by the Park and Activities Commission at its February meeting.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  4
March 24, 2024
   She stated that any fee changes proposed by the Committee would be presented
  to the Park and Activities Commission before being forwarded for consideration to
  City Council. She reported that staff was working to secure a consultant to conduct
  a fee study for all recreation programs and that the fees were being proposed in
  accordance with current policy.

  No changes were proposed as there was a consensus that the proposed fees were
  reasonable.

  G.  MAY MEETING DATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas informed the committee that the date for the regular
  meeting set for May falls on Memorial Day. She proposed the Committee consider
  an alternate date and recommended the consideration of Monday, May 19.

  There was a consensus to move the May meeting date to Monday, May 19, 2025.

  H.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  NONE.

  D.  MATTERS OF INTEREST

  NONE.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  MAYOR’S RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the item.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the event was scheduled for Saturday, May 10. She
  reported that the Scouts would return to host the pancake breakfast, that invitations
  to the Committee Members had gone out earlier that day and welcomed them to
  participate in the ride and breakfast.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ thanked the Committee for helping advertise the event and
  emphasized the importance of publicizing the event to maintain attendance and
  keep such activities thriving.

  B.  PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM PROJECT UPDATE
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis provided a brief overview of the item.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  5
March 24, 2024
   She reported that the main bathroom had been closed a couple years ago due to
  sewer issues and that the project has encountered challenges due to requirements
  from the Los Angeles County Public Health Local Enforcement Agency. She
  reviewed the process to date including hiring a consultant to complete the Post
  Closure Land Use Plan. She stated that the Plan was completed and that additional
  methane monitoring around the site may be necessary. She reported that the City
  is actively working with Supervisor Hahn’s office to navigate these requirements
  and is exploring opportunities to secure additional funding. She stated that
  temporary trailer-type porta-potties are being considered while the process
  continues.

  MEMBER ROMANELLI expressed concern regarding the ongoing delays and
  recommended convening a comprehensive meeting with all involved parties to
  address the outstanding issues. ACM Davis stated that all relevant parties have
  now been engaged, and that progress is being made on the project.

  C.  EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith reported that the Fern Creek Trail had
  been closed due to a hole caused by drainage problems, with repairs anticipated to
  take approximately one week once work begins.

  In response to MEMBER HARIK, Superintendent Goldsmith stated that castor bean
  plants are toxic to horses, and have been identified in certain areas, particularly
  where property owners use a landscaping method called discing. He stated that
  castor bean is not prevalent around the City’s bridle trails and that there is only one
  City parcel that is disked and that the others are mowed. He stated that the only
  way to get rid of castor bean plants is to remove them by pulling the plants out by
  the root.

  In response to MEMBER SHINN, Superintendent Goldsmith stated that new jumps
  are now available for placement in equestrian arenas and asked the Committee
  Members for suggestions regarding locations to place the new jumps. MEMBER
  SHINN suggested some be placed in the Chandler Park arena.

  In response to MEMBER GRIGGS, ACM Davis stated that she was not aware of
  whether the City received advance notice of Palos Verdes Estates’ use of goats for
  brush clearance but was aware that they were considering it. She stated that she
  believed their timeline may have been moved up sooner than expected.

  CHAIR SCHMITZ commented on the fire prevention work needed in Palos Verdes
  Estates and that the use of the goats was a way to get fire prevention work done
  quickly.

  D.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES  6
March 24, 2024
   NONE.

  8.  COMMITTEE REPORTS

  A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  9.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:04 p.m.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,
